summary: Sorting is about ordering, but the interview value is the machinery around it: the merge step (two-pointer combine of sorted runs), partitioning (split around a pivot), counting (bucket by value when the range is small), and comparators (define 'order' for anything). Master the merge and partition routines and most sorting problems are variations — inversion counting, wave arrays, closest points, custom-key sorts.

thoughtProcess.title: 1. Ask: is the value range small?
thoughtProcess.body: If values fit a small range (colors 0-2, digits, bounded ints), a counting/bucket sort is O(N + range) and beats comparison sorts. Reach for it before merge/quick.

thoughtProcess.title: 2. Reach for the merge step as a Swiss-army knife.
thoughtProcess.body: Merging two sorted runs with two pointers underlies merge sort, 'merge two sorted arrays', and inversion counting (count left-leftovers when a right element is taken). If a problem smells like 'combine sorted things' or 'count out-of-order pairs', think merge.

thoughtProcess.title: 3. Partition when you need a pivot boundary.
thoughtProcess.body: Quick sort, partition-index, and Dutch-flag all rearrange around a pivot/value. Keep a boundary pointer and sweep. Watch the pivot placement and the <= vs < tie rules.

thoughtProcess.title: 4. When order is custom, write a comparator.
thoughtProcess.body: Largest-number (a+b vs b+a), factors sort, tens-digit sort, closest-points — the whole problem is defining the comparator. State the primary key and the tie-break explicitly, and cast to long when squaring/concatenating to avoid overflow.

keyPatterns.name: Two-pointer merge
keyPatterns.when: Combine two sorted runs / count inversions

keyPatterns.name: Counting / bucket
keyPatterns.when: Values in a small bounded range
keyPatterns.template:
count[v]++ for all v
emit v, count[v] times, v ascending

keyPatterns.name: Partition around pivot
keyPatterns.template:
boundary i=0
for j: if A[j]<pivot swap(i,j), i++
swap pivot into i

keyPatterns.name: Custom comparator
keyPatterns.when: Order defined by a derived key

commonMistakes.title: Seeding max/answer wrong or overflow on keys
commonMistakes.wrong: int d = x*x + y*y;   // int overflow for large coords

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting the all-zeros / leading-zero guard
commonMistakes.wrong: return concatenation;            // returns "000" for all zeros

edgeCases: All elements equal (partition degenerates — watch <= vs < in the sweep).
Already sorted or reverse sorted (quick sort worst case O(N^2) with fixed pivot).
Single element or empty window (base cases in recursion / [B,C] with B==C).
Large coordinates/values — use long for squared distance and concatenations.
